sanskrit: yaṃ gṛhṇanty apsaraso yaṃ mathnāti bṛhaspatiḥ | taṃ kaśyapasya brahmaṇā savitā punar ā bharat ||
english: Him whom the Apsarases seize, whom Bṛhaspati afflicts by churning — him may Savitṛ bring back again by the brahman of Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: yo bhartākūḥ paridhāya mṛgeṣv api dhāvati | taṃ kaśyapasya brahmaṇā savitā punar ā bharat ||
english: He who, having taken on the guise of a beast-carrier, runs about among the wild animals — him may Savitṛ bring back again by the brahman of Kaśyapa.

sanskrit: savitāgnir brahmā soma indras tvaṣṭā bṛhaspatiḥ | ete marudyutaṃ tvā brahmaṇā punar ā bharan ||
english: Savitṛ, Agni, Brahmā, Soma, Indra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Bṛhaspati — these have brought thee back, O Marudyuta, by the brahman.

sanskrit: bhadrāṃ vācaṃ śivaṃ cakṣur marudyutāya kṛṇmasi | imāṃ hy asmā oṣadhim ā harāmy arundhatīm ||
english: Auspicious speech and a wholesome eye — these we fashion for Marudyuta; for him indeed I bring this herb, Arundhatī.

sanskrit: tribhyo rudrebhyaḥ pravasan yajāmi jyeṣṭhaḥ kaniṣṭha uta madhyamo yaḥ | jyotiṣkārāḥ kavayaḥ somapā ye kaṇvā ajantu nir ito vadhena ||
english: To the three Rudras — the eldest, the youngest, and him who is the middlemost — I make oblation as I set forth; the light-makers, the seers, the soma-drinkers — let them drive the Kaṇvās out from here with the weapon.

sanskrit: indrāgnī vītaṃ haviṣaḥ saṃvidānau samiddho agniḥ samidhā gīrbhir indraḥ | nudethāṃ kaṇvā nir ito arātim ārād rakṣāṃsi tapataṃ vy asmat ||
english: O Indra and Agni, come to the oblation, in accord with one another — Agni kindled with fuel, Indra kindled with hymns — drive the Kaṇvās and ill-will out from here; burn the demons far away from us.

sanskrit: vāstoṣpate suprajasaḥ suvīrā ṣaṣṭhīsyāmi śaradaḥ śatāni | durvāstu kaṇvā abhi nir ṇudasva suvāstv asmām̐ upa saṃ viśasva ||
english: O Vāstoṣpati, lord of the homestead, [grant us] good offspring and good heroes — I shall live out six hundred autumns; drive the ill-dwelling Kaṇvās away on all sides; enter into us bringing a good abode.

sanskrit: yā tantiṣat khalasad yā ca goṣṭhe yā jātāḥ śakadhūme sabhāyām | prapāyāṃ jātā uta yāś ca bhitsu tāś cātayāmaḥ śivatā no astu ||
english: Those [Kaṇvās] that settled on the loom-thread, that sat on the threshing-floor, and those in the cowpen, those born amid the smoke of dung-fire, those in the assembly hall, those born at the watering-place and those among the clefts — these we drive away; may auspiciousness be ours.

sanskrit: dudvā ca dudvatī ca sthas tad vāṃ nāma tad vāṃ nāmadheyam | rudrapreṣite stho 'vye nāma pary asmān vṛṅktam | yo no dveṣṭi tam ṛcchatam ||
english: Ye two are Dudvā and Dudvatī — that is your name, that is your appellation; sent by Rudra, ye two bear the name Avya — ward off [evil] from around us; him who hates us, do ye strike.

sanskrit: vīcī nāmāsy aghahārā nāma | namas te astu vātake 'nyatrāsmad aghaṃ kṛdhi ||
english: Thou art named Vīcī, named Aghahārā — homage be to thee, O Vātaka; cause the evil to fall elsewhere, away from us.

sanskrit: ṛjīte pari ṇo nama- -agreṇa pari ṇo nama | aśmānaṃ tanvaṃ kṛṇmahe adyā naḥ soma mṛḍaya ||
english: O Ṛjīta, homage around us — homage around us from the fore; we make our bodies [hard as] stone; today, O Soma, be gracious to us.

sanskrit: tvaṃ darbhāsi patir oṣadhīnāṃ vibhindan yāsi kanyā ivainām | bhindhi śiraḥ kṛmer jāyānyasya śarīraṃ bhindhy uta bhindhy asthi ||
english: Thou art Darbha, the lord of plants; going, thou dost cleave it open as a maiden would; split the head of the worm, [split] the mate of another's worm — split the body and split indeed the bone.

sanskrit: yaḥ kīkasāstho viradāt parūṃṣi yasyoddhāra uṣṇihās tā hi vavre | haniṣyāmi vāṃ nir ataḥ paretaṃ tṛṇāny attam avasīriṇām iva ||
english: That [worm] which, lodged in the ribs, splits apart the joints, whose discharge stopped up the Uṣṇihā vessels — those were indeed covered over — I will smite you two; go forth and be gone from here; eat the grasses of the weaning-cows [far from here].

sanskrit: ayaṃ ya āste jaṭhareṣv antaḥ kāsphīvaśaṃ nirajaṃ martyasya | haniṣyāmi vāṃ nir ataḥ paretaṃ stāyad eyathuḥ prati vām abhutsi ||
english: This one that lurks within the belly-cavities as the foul, ulcer-less affliction of a mortal — I will smite you two; go forth and be gone from here; O stealthily-creeping pair, your movement I have blocked.

sanskrit: yeneyathus tena pathā paretaṃ stāyad eyathuḥ prati vām abhutsi | brahmaṇā vāṃ paritṛhya samantaṃ vi cchetsyāmi nakula iva sarpam ||
english: By that very path along which ye two have crept — go forth and be gone from there; O stealthily-creeping pair, your movement I have blocked; enclosing you two all around with the brahman, I will cut you asunder, as the mongoose [cuts] the serpent.
